quests.instruction: A colleague presents a very tight schedule, and you're doubtful.
quests.word: That's certainly an ambitious timeline.
quests.textToSpeak: That's certainly an ambitious timeline.
options: Slight stress on 'certainly', level fall — polite doubt
Warm peak on 'ambitious', wide fall — real admiration
quests.correctAnswer: Slight stress on 'certainly', level fall — polite doubt
quests.hint: 'Ambitious' can be a compliment or a warning. Which delivery hints at the second?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'certainly' with a level fall suggests reservation. A warm peak on 'ambitious' would sound admiring.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Polite doubt hides in a level fall.

quests.instruction: Your colleague's plan isn't ideal, but you'll go along with it.
quests.word: Well, I suppose that works.
quests.textToSpeak: Well, I suppose that works.
options: Low, slow fall — grudging acceptance
Bright, quick fall — pleased acceptance
quests.correctAnswer: Low, slow fall — grudging acceptance
quests.hint: The phrase 'I suppose' already hints at reluctance. Which delivery matches?
quests.explanation: A low, slow fall signals that the speaker isn't happy. A bright fall would give the opposite message.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Grudging acceptance is slow and low.

quests.instruction: A colleague has clearly rushed a report, and hands it in with a smile.
quests.word: You've clearly put a lot of thought into this.
quests.textToSpeak: You've clearly put a lot of thought into this.
options: Flat, stress on 'clearly' — ironic
Warm rise-fall on 'lot' — sincere
quests.correctAnswer: Flat, stress on 'clearly' — ironic
quests.hint: Compare what the words say with what the situation suggests.
quests.explanation: Stress on 'clearly' and a flat fall turn the praise into irony. A warm peak on 'lot' would be sincere.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Flat stress on an adverb can signal irony.

quests.instruction: You arrive at eight and hint at someone who didn't.
quests.word: Some of us were here at eight.
quests.textToSpeak: Some of us were here at eight.
options: Peak on 'eight', falling tone — factual time report
Stress on 'some', level tone — implied criticism
quests.correctAnswer: Stress on 'some', level tone — implied criticism
quests.hint: The speaker points at a contrast between people. Which word carries it?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'some' sets a group against another, which implies criticism. Peak on 'eight' would state a time.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on a pronoun can imply a comparison between people.

quests.instruction: You hint that you did think the idea was bad, but stayed quiet.
quests.word: I didn't say it was a bad idea.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't say it was a bad idea.
options: Peak on 'say' — implies 'but I thought it'
Peak on 'bad' — implies 'it was a different kind of idea'
quests.correctAnswer: Peak on 'say' — implies 'but I thought it'
quests.hint: The speaker denies one thing but hints at another. Which word shows that?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'say' implies that the speaker thought it without saying it. Stress on 'bad' would imply a different kind of criticism.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on 'say' implies an unspoken thought.

quests.instruction: A visitor asks if they can walk to the station, and you'd rather they didn't.
quests.word: It's quite a walk from here.
quests.textToSpeak: It's quite a walk from here.
options: Stress on 'quite', slight lift — implies 'not advisable'
Level fall, no stress — just describing the distance
quests.correctAnswer: Stress on 'quite', slight lift — implies 'not advisable'
quests.hint: You are giving more than information. Which delivery hints at it?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'quite' with a slight lift leaves 'so maybe don't' unspoken. A level fall would only describe.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 A slight lift leaves an implication hanging.

quests.instruction: A colleague has missed deadlines before and promises again.
quests.word: He said he'd have it ready by Friday.
quests.textToSpeak: He said he'd have it ready by Friday.
options: Peak on 'Friday' — highlighting the date
Stress on 'said', level end — doubt

quests.explanation: Stress on 'said' distances the speaker from the promise. A peak on 'Friday' would highlight the deadline instead.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on the reporting verb can signal doubt.

quests.instruction: The parcel has been late every time before.
quests.word: Oh, I'm sure it'll arrive on time.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh, I'm sure it'll arrive on time.
options: Warm fall on 'time', no stress — confident
Stress on 'sure', flat fall — doubting

quests.hint: The past experience matters. Which delivery matches it?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'sure' with a flat fall gives away the speaker's doubt. A warm fall would sound confident.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on 'sure' can signal doubt.

quests.instruction: A friend repeats a company's empty promise.
quests.word: That's what they always say.
quests.textToSpeak: That's what they always say.
options: Rising — asking
Low, flat fall — cynical

quests.hint: The speaker has heard this before. Which delivery is weary?
quests.explanation: A low, flat fall shows cynicism. A rise would ask a question.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Cynicism drops and flattens.

quests.instruction: A colleague you expected later walks in.
quests.word: Oh, you're already here.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh, you're already here.

Wide peak on 'already' — big shock

quests.explanation: A small lift on 'already' shows mild surprise. A wide peak would signal astonishment.

quests.instruction: A friend reveals something that is new but not thrilling.
quests.word: Huh, I didn't know that.
quests.textToSpeak: Huh, I didn't know that.

High start, wide fall — real excitement

quests.explanation: A small range on 'that' shows quiet interest. A high fall would sound excited.

quests.instruction: The bill arrives and it's higher than you expected.
quests.word: That's a bit more than I expected.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a bit more than I expected.
options: Bright rise-fall — pleasantly surprised
Stress on 'more', lowered fall — mildly unwelcome

quests.explanation: A lowered fall with stress on 'more' expresses mild disappointment. A bright rise-fall would sound pleased.
quests.pitchRule: 😲 Unwelcome surprise lowers the pitch.

quests.instruction: A colleague shows you a decent mockup, and you're pleased but reserved.
quests.word: That'd be pretty good, actually.
quests.textToSpeak: That'd be pretty good, actually.

Small lift on 'good', quick fall — understated pleasure

quests.explanation: A small lift and a quick fall show that you like it without gushing. A wide rise-fall would exaggerate.

quests.instruction: The results are acceptable and you feel a quiet satisfaction.
quests.word: Not a bad result, all things considered.
quests.textToSpeak: Not a bad result, all things considered.
options: High start, wide fall — jubilant celebration
Level start, gentle fall — restrained satisfaction

quests.hint: You are satisfied but not celebrating. Which delivery fits?
quests.explanation: A level start and gentle fall show contained satisfaction. A wide fall would signal celebration.

quests.instruction: You've accomplished something you expected to be hard.
quests.word: I'm quite pleased with how it turned out.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm quite pleased with how it turned out.
options: Slight lift on 'quite', warm fall — modest pride
Bright peak on 'pleased' — bursting pride
quests.correctAnswer: Slight lift on 'quite', warm fall — modest pride
quests.hint: The word 'quite' softens the pride. Which delivery keeps it modest?
quests.explanation: A slight lift and a warm fall show modest pride. A bright peak would suggest bragging.
quests.pitchRule: 😊 Modest pride uses a small lift and a warm fall.

quests.instruction: You object to a proposal while sounding open.
quests.word: That could work, though I'm wondering about the cost.
quests.textToSpeak: That could work, though I'm wondering about the cost.
options: Lift on 'work', lift on 'wondering', fall on 'cost' — cautious objection
Fall on 'work', 'wondering' and 'cost' — flat rejection
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'work', lift on 'wondering', fall on 'cost' — cautious objection
quests.hint: You want to raise a concern without blocking. Which delivery sounds open?
quests.explanation: The lifts keep the tone tentative and the fall on 'cost' delivers the concern. Two falls would sound like rejection.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝 Indirect objections keep lifts before the concern.

quests.instruction: You'd like to suggest more options without criticizing.
quests.word: Maybe we could look at other options too?
quests.textToSpeak: Maybe we could look at other options too?

Rising — softened objection

quests.hint: You don't want to appear negative. Which ending is gentle?
quests.explanation: A rise on 'too' turns the objection into a suggestion. A fall would sound like an instruction.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝📈 A rise softens an objection.

quests.instruction: You don't agree, but you're avoiding a direct no.
quests.word: I'm not sure that's the direction we want.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not sure that's the direction we want.
options: Stress on 'sure', lifted end — indirect no
Firm fall on 'want' — direct no

quests.explanation: Stress on 'sure' and a lifted end invite discussion. A firm fall would sound like a decision.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝 A lifted end keeps an indirect no open.

quests.instruction: You see a colleague in a very casual outfit before a client meeting.
quests.word: Is that what you're wearing?
quests.textToSpeak: Is that what you're wearing?
options: Stress on 'wearing', rising — asks about the outfit type
Stress on 'that', rising — implies criticism

quests.instruction: A friend gets up to leave the party earlier than expected.

Stress on 'already', rising — disappointed

Stress on 'make', rising — suspecting a purchase
